chunks: Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to administer eighty lashes for intoxicating nabidh, just as he would administer for wine, and he would execute on the third offense just as he would execute the wine-drinker.

key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty; the number of lashes prescribed here
key_terms.صَاحِبَ ٱلْخَمْرِ: the wine-drinker; the one who drinks wine and whose ruling is used as the comparison
key_terms.ٱلثَّالِثَةِ: the third time; indicating the third offense
key_terms.ٱلنَّبِيذِ: nabidh; a fermented drink, here specifically in its intoxicating form
key_terms.ٱلْخَمْرِ: wine; the standard intoxicant to which the ruling is compared

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking intoxicating nabidh in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام treated intoxicating nabidh with the same hadd punishment as wine. It also indicates that the repeated offender is punished on the third offense in the same manner as the habitual wine-drinker.
